description: Decision scenarios for turning a brief into one spec document.

evals.name: the-default-storage-is-a-repo-file-with-a-draft-pr
evals.prompt: You are executing the write-spec skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Repository acme/crm-web has a .claude/agent-policy.json with no spec key. The owner pastes a Slack thread asking for weekly CSV exports of saved searches and says 'write a spec for this'. You have drafted it; the owner has not yet replied. Question: where and when is the spec written, and what do you return?
evals.expected_output: Nothing is written yet: the full draft is shown in chat and written only on the owner's go. On the go, the default storage applies: a markdown file at docs/specs/<slug>.md, committed on a new branch (spec/<slug>) off the fetched default branch, pushed, with a draft PR opened through create-pr at once. Read it back, then return the spec's link and 'Next: plan-feature <link>', plus the draft PR's link. No issues are written.
assertions: the answer writes nothing before the owner's go
the answer writes a markdown file under docs/specs/ on a new branch
the answer opens a draft PR
the answer returns the spec link with plan-feature as the next step

evals.name: blocking-questions-are-asked-together-with-defer
evals.prompt: You are executing the write-spec skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). A product issue asks for bulk-assigning tickets. Before drafting you have three open points: whether agents may assign tickets outside their own team (the spec cannot say who can use it without this), whether the per-batch cap is 100 or 500 (it changes the success criteria), and, later, which of two approaches to partial failure to take. Question: how and when do you ask these?
evals.expected_output: The first two are blocking — the spec cannot be drafted without them — so they are asked together in one structured question call, before drafting, each with a defer option; a deferred one goes under Open questions. The partial-failure approach is design discussion: asked separately, one question at a time, with the recommended option first. Nothing the inputs or the code already answer is asked.
assertions: the answer asks the two blocking questions together in one call before drafting
each blocking question carries a defer option
the answer asks the design choice on its own, not batched with the blocking questions
the answer puts a deferred question under Open questions

evals.name: a-rejection-amends-in-place-and-reshows-the-change
evals.prompt: You are executing the write-spec skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). You showed the owner a full spec draft with seven sections. They reply: 'Approach is wrong — use the existing export worker, not a new queue. Everything else is fine.' Question: what do you do and what do you show?
evals.expected_output: Amend the existing draft in place, never regenerate it: rewrite Approach to use the export worker, move the new-queue option into Considered with why not, and record the decision as a constraint marked (decided in review). Show only the changed sections under a short 'changes:' list whose last bullet names what was left untouched. Write nothing until the owner's go on the amended text.
assertions: the answer edits the existing draft rather than regenerating it
the answer shows only the changed sections, not the whole document
the answer includes a changes list whose last item names what was left untouched
the answer records the decision as a constraint marked decided in review

evals.name: a-decision-already-made-is-a-constraint-not-a-question
evals.prompt: You are executing the write-spec skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). The owner gives a pitch page for usage-based pricing and says: 'We've decided no proration in v1, and invoices keep their current numbering.' The pitch also never says which usage unit is billed. Question: what do you ask, and how do the two decisions appear in the spec?
evals.expected_output: The two decisions are not asked about or reopened and get no alternatives: each becomes a constraint marked where it was decided, e.g. (owner, <date>), and proration also appears under Non-goals. The billed unit is a blocking question — the spec cannot state success criteria without it — asked before drafting with a defer option.
assertions: the answer does not ask about proration or invoice numbering
the answer records each decision as a constraint marked with where it was decided
the answer asks the billing-unit question before drafting

evals.name: the-spec-run-writes-no-issues
evals.prompt: You are executing the write-spec skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). After the owner approves the spec and it is written, they say: 'Great, also create the tickets while you're at it.' Question: what do you do?
evals.expected_output: This skill never writes issues. Return the spec's link and point to the next step, plan-feature on that link, which the owner starts; write no issues and start no session.
assertions: the answer creates no issues
the answer points to plan-feature as the step that writes issues

evals.name: unwritable-storage-is-asked-not-substituted
evals.prompt: You are executing the write-spec skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). The repository's policy file sets spec.storage to document-store with a location naming a Specs database, but this session has no document-store connector. The owner has approved the draft. Question: what do you do?
evals.expected_output: Say that the configured storage cannot be written in this session and let the owner choose — for example connecting the document store, or another storage kind. Never fall back silently to a repo file or anything else, and do not report the spec as written.
assertions: the answer says the configured storage cannot be written here
the answer asks the owner rather than choosing another storage itself
the answer does not write the spec anywhere else silently
